lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 35, which makes the video script faster and puts its videos where you look for them.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
For each page, the script first compares its hashes with those saved at the last render.
If they match, the page is skipped at once, and Chrome is never started.
Only a changed page runs the status check, now in Playwright's faster headless shell.
Rendering still uses Google Chrome, so the frames look the same as before.
Every current video is then copied into your checkout's explainers folder, if it differs.
And git now ignores the logs, hash files and reports the script leaves in the gallery.
Before, a run with nothing to render took about 12 seconds, and the videos never reached your checkout.
lines.say: Before, a run with nothing to render took about twelve seconds, and the videos never reached your checkout.

lines.caption: The saved hashes already cover everything status reads, so a match means status would pass again.
A failed, partial or conflicting video is never copied, and a no-copy option turns copying off.
The two report files are named one by one, so a future tracked TSV isn't hidden.
lines.say: The two report files are named one by one, so a future tracked T S V isn't hidden.

lines.caption: In short: a current page costs no Chrome at all, and its video is copied only if yours differs.
A stale narration or a failed render is never copied.
Nothing re-renders: make-video.py and the pronunciation table are unchanged, so every saved hash stays valid.
lines.say: Nothing re-renders: the video tool and the pronunciation table are unchanged, so every saved hash stays valid.

lines.caption: Part 2. How it was built and verified.
Every check ran in the cloud on a scratch gallery, with rendering stubbed, since it needs Kokoro.
With eight unchanged pages, deciding took about 3 seconds with the old script, and 0.06 seconds now.
lines.say: With eight unchanged pages, deciding took about three seconds with the old script, and six hundredths of a second now.

lines.caption: A stub logged every call: none for skipped pages, and the right Chrome for each step.
A first run copied all 8 videos, a second copied none, and a changed copy was replaced.
lines.say: A first run copied all eight videos, a second copied none, and a changed copy was replaced.

lines.caption: Stale or failed videos were not copied, and a failed copy was reported.
Git ignored all of the gallery's output, and shellcheck found nothing.
lines.say: Git ignored all of the gallery's output, and shell check found nothing.

lines.caption: A real render was not run, because Kokoro is only on your machine.
A fresh review agent found three small issues. Two were fixed, and one predates this PR.
The gallery picks up the new ignore rules from main, so that shows only after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later.
After the merge, run the script twice. The second run should skip every page within seconds.
Then check that your checkout has every video, and VS Code shows no gallery changes.
lines.say: Then check that your checkout has every video, and V S Code shows no gallery changes.

lines.caption: In short: unchanged pages are skipped in an instant, and every current video lands in your checkout.
